title: "How to use this playbook"
description: "Who it is for, how it is organised, and how to find things quickly."
---

This playbook sets out how analysis is planned, produced, assured and communicated at NHSBSA.

## If you are in a hurry

Most people arrive with one question: **how much assurance does this piece of work need, and what do
I actually have to do?**

1. [Decide your assurance level](../05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). Five minutes.
2. [Find what it requires](../06-doing-the-work/index.qmd). Read the column for your level.

That is the whole path. Everything else here exists for when you need it.

If you would rather see the whole route for your role before you start,
[journeys through this playbook](journeys.qmd) has one diagram each for the analyst, the
commissioner, the critical friend and the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer.

## Who it is for

- **Directors and Heads of Service**, to ensure appropriate governance of analysis in their areas
- **Commissioners** requesting analysis, including non-analysts and third-party suppliers
- **Analysts** producing it, and the **critical friends** assuring it

## What it covers

**All of it.** NHSBSA takes an analytical output in the broadest sense: an output that results from
the collection, manipulation and interpretation of data to answer specific questions. That runs from
a dataset created in answer to a Freedom of Information request or a Parliamentary Question, through
a sponsor's request for data to inform a policy decision, an official statistics report and a
dashboard for commissioners, to a complex forecasting model informing budgets. Used internally,
supplied to sponsors, or published externally: all of it is in scope.[^src-operating-model-outputs]

Those are examples rather than a checklist, and there is no central record of everything NHSBSA
produces, so the test is the definition rather than the list. If you collected, manipulated or
interpreted data to answer a question, and somebody is going to act on the answer, this playbook
applies to it.

What changes between them is how much assurance each one needs, and that is
[section 5](../05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). NHSBSA's own worked examples are there,
from exploratory analysis at Level 1 to a funding allocation formula at Level 4, along with the
eight types an analytical model can be.

## How it is organised

Fifteen sections. The sidebar carries every one of them in this order, on every page, so
nothing here is reachable only from a link inside another page.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-playbook-map.qmd >}}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/section-contents.qmd >}}

Section 8 is the one section that gathers rather than adds. Being Business Critical changes what
happens at seven points in the lifecycle, and each of those points belongs to the section that
owns it, so section 8 puts them in the order you meet them and includes each passage from its
owner rather than copying it. The two cannot drift apart.

## Giving feedback

This playbook is maintained and it is meant to change. If something here is wrong, unclear, or does
not match how work actually happens, say so. [Section 13](../13-getting-help/index.qmd) has the
route.
